raw_response:
I've been working this land for forty years. I know what Quzhou soil wants, I know the weather here, and I know what sells. My wife and I have two mouths to feed and a small farm — every mu counts.

**My thinking this season:**

Cotton is my backbone. Quzhou is cotton country — the buyers come here, I know the local dealers, and I've grown it since I was young. I'll put most of my land into cotton. I'll use the hybrid Bt seed I've been using the past several years — the bollworm pressure here is serious and I can't afford to lose a crop to that. I know some old farmers still use traditional seed but I've seen what happens. I'll do rotary tillage in early April before transplanting, apply base fertilizer, then topdress during the boll-setting stage. We'll need to irrigate — the well gives us good water — probably four times through the season: germination, flowering, boll-setting, and if July is dry. I'll spray for aphids and bollworm as needed, likely five times.

Stevia I've been growing a few years now. It brings decent money and the leaf buyers come around in late summer. I'll keep it to 2 mu — I understand it well enough now. It doesn't need as much fertilizer as cotton, but I still need to irrigate it a few times in the dry months. Pest pressure is lighter on stevia so I won't spray as much.

I won't experiment this year. I'm 64, I know what works.
